name: Hunza
description: A long, green valley under some of the highest mountains on earth: terraced orchards, the old forts of Baltit and Altit, and the turquoise of Attabad Lake.
lead: Forts, orchards and the Karakoram, three days up the highway from Lahore

image.alt: Rakaposhi’s snowy face above a Hunza village and terraced fields lined with yellow autumn poplars

overview.headline: A green valley under the highest peaks
paragraphs: Hunza is a long, green valley under some of the highest mountains on earth. Terraced fields and apricot orchards climb towards Rakaposhi and Ultar, and the old forts of Baltit and Altit still watch over the villages.

People come for the views and stay for the pace: short walks between orchards, chai facing the glaciers, and the turquoise of Attabad Lake further up the highway. For many first-timers, it is where they fall for the north.

seasons.text: Apricot and cherry blossom from early April. Days 15–22°C, nights near freezing early in the season.
Warm days, 25–30°C, and the busiest months. Book four to six weeks ahead.
The poplars turn gold in late October. Days 10–20°C, cold nights.
Snow on the Karakoram Highway, and many hotels close. Days around 5°C, nights down to −10°C.

places.name: Baltit Fort
places.text: The centuries-old fort above Karimabad, restored and open to visitors.

image.alt: Whitewashed walls and carved red wooden balconies of Baltit Fort rise above a stone terrace under a deep blue sky.

places.name: Altit Fort
places.text: Older still, on a cliff above the river, with a royal garden below.

image.alt: The stone tower of Altit Fort rises from a granite outcrop against a deep blue sky, beside poplar-covered mountain slopes.

places.name: Eagle’s Nest
places.text: Sunset over Rakaposhi, Ultar and Lady Finger from the ridge at Duikar.

image.alt: The green Hunza valley seen from the ridge at Eagle’s Nest, with poplars in front and snowy peaks along the skyline

places.name: Attabad Lake
places.text: Turquoise lake formed by the 2010 landslide; boats leave from the jetty.

image.alt: Turquoise water of Attabad Lake filling the gorge below grey scree slopes and a blue sky

places.name: Passu Cones
places.text: Jagged spires above the highway in upper Hunza.

image.alt: The jagged spires of the Passu Cones catch evening light under heavy clouds, with poplars on a dark hillside below.

places.name: Hussaini Bridge
places.text: A swaying suspension bridge over the Hunza River. Not for everyone.

image.alt: The empty Hussaini suspension bridge stretches over the grey Hunza River toward a sheer rock cliff and jagged peaks.

places.name: Rakaposhi viewpoint
places.text: A roadside tea stop facing one of the world’s great mountain faces.

image.alt: Snow-covered Rakaposhi above the Hunza valley at sunset, with golden autumn poplars below
